central_topic: Evidence-bounded prediction of LLM full binary benchmark scores and rankings from fixed 8-, 16-, or 32-item prefixes using source-only score-covariance selection and ridge/Rasch-residual reconstruction; incremental citation support is needed only for upstream Open LLM Leaderboard collection context and Rasch/2PL foundations.
core_methods: Source-only score-targeted fixed nested prefixes with grouped tuning and ridge score reconstruction; existing methodological citations require no new search
Rasch ability-minus-difficulty response probabilities used to smooth source profiles; direct model-family foundations are missing at paper.tex:86
Fixed-ability, group-weighted penalized fitting and optional residual-profile blending remain artifact-grounded custom implementation details, not claims licensed by a foundational citation
comparators: The local penalized two-parameter logistic comparator uses item discrimination and fitted Fisher item information; foundational support is needed at paper.tex:130 and paper.tex:293
Anchor Points, tinyBenchmarks, metabench, reference-instance prediction, and active evaluation acquisition already have direct citations; no comparator-family expansion is needed
benchmarks: Open LLM Leaderboard-derived final cases BBH, GPQA, MuSR, and OpenLLM Math need one authoritative upstream collection reference at paper.tex:115; staged identities, counts, filtering, and snapshot details remain artifact-grounded

HELM-derived final cases Commonsense, GSM, LegalBench, MATH, MedQA, and MMLU need no new retrieval; reuse Liang2023 for HELM collection context, and do not use Wang2024 (MMLU-Pro) as provenance for staged MMLU
result_driven_themes: Completed but unqualified evaluation, missing predictions, structural diagnostics, and retained-support results are artifact-grounded; additional references cannot repair or explain them
No citation enrichment should imply selector superiority, an isolated residual-profile benefit, calibrated target uncertainty, or official reproduction of a published comparator

queries.query: Rasch logistic item-response model ability item difficulty foundational reference
queries.rationale: Fills method-rasch-irt-foundations at Method / Linear and Residual-Profile Reconstruction, specifically 'The nonlinear branch retains source response profiles while smoothing them with a Rasch model.' (paper.tex:86). Seek an authoritative foundation for the logistic ability-minus-difficulty response family, preferably also explaining the 2PL distinction and item information so the source can be reused for the local comparator. Andersen1970 is already cited specifically for conditional maximum-likelihood estimation, which the draft does not use; its stored abstract does not directly close this model-family gap. Do not characterize the fixed-ability penalized custom fit as standard joint Rasch estimation or infer empirical profile benefit.

queries.query: two-parameter logistic item-response model discrimination Fisher item information authoritative reference
queries.rationale: Conditional complement within method-rasch-irt-foundations: execute only if the Rasch source does not also support the local 2PL comparator in Evaluation Protocol and Evidence Availability / Comparators and Control Semantics (paper.tex:130) and Supplementary Information / Local Reference Implementations (paper.tex:293). Seek at most one complementary authoritative source for variable discrimination and Fisher information a^2 p(1-p), checking consistency with the draft's theta*a-d parameterization. This is model-family framing, not a new comparator search or evidence that the local penalized fit reproduces tinyBenchmarks or another published package.
